item.title: Senior Day: BYU will honor these 21 players on Saturday before hosting Cincinnati, although a few may return
item.description: BYU running back Lj Martin (4) celebrates after scoring a touchdown during overtime of an NCAA college football game against Kansas, Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026, in Lawrence, Kan. | Charlie Riedel, Associated Press Up to 21 BYU football players will make their final appearances at LaVell Edwards Stadium on Saturday before the No. 10 Cougars host Cincinnati in another pivotal Big 12 game. The players will be recognized on Senior Day (1:30 p.m. MST, Fox) for their contributions to the program in the final home game of the 2026 season and receive blankets from the school for their service to the team. Star running back LJ Martin, who is in his fourth season in Provo, is on the list, as expected. Appearing via Zoom in BYU’s weekly press briefing on Monday, Martin acknowledged that it will likely be his final game at LES, although technically he could return in 2027 via the NCAA’s new “age-based eligibility model” — commonly referred to as the “five-for-five” rule . “Yeah, this is probably my last time (playing at BYU),” Martin said. “I played four years here, had a lot of fun. Had a lot of great times. We’ll just see how things go. Just excited for the game Saturday. Haven’t really thought about it or anything. Just trying to go out there, focus on Saturday, just have a great game, and we’ll see where that goes.” Martin carried the ball a season-high 25 times for 127 yards and a touchdown in BYU’s 31-29 win over Kansas last weekend in his first significant playing time since sustaining a high ankle sprain on Oct. 3 at TCU. He said he was “just sore” on Sunday, but otherwise came out of the game “feeling pretty good” and looking forward to building on it. Martin seriously considered leaving BYU for the NFL last year after earning Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year honors, but opted to stay after receiving input from the league on his projected draft status. He said he will go through the same process this year. “I will probably just talk to my parents, probably a couple guys here (at BYU), and just try to get feedback from the NFL, I guess,” he said. “Just kind of feel it out and see what I want to do with my future.” Also Monday, head coach Kalani Sitake recapped the three-overtime win over Kansas , said an almost healthy Martin made a huge difference for an offense that had struggled to run the football in recent weeks, and looked ahead to facing a Cincinnati team (6-5, 3-5) that snapped a three-game losing skid with a 35-28 win over Colorado last Saturday. “It was good to see LJ back to his old self,” Sitake said. “I think that last (touchdown) run was probably the LJ that we’ve been waiting for. Two weeks ago (vs. Baylor) he got stepped on, and last week he got pulled on, on that (surgically repaired) leg. item.title: Georgia Tech Coach Brent Key Promises Fight Against UGA Rivalry
item.description: Ashley Tumlin-Imagn Images The Georgia Bulldogs are heading into their annual rivalry game against the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets with a massive lead in the standings. Georgia finished the SEC schedule on top and is set for its sixth straight conference title game appearance. This matchup is known as Clean, Old-Fashioned Hate, but the dynamic has shifted significantly this year. Georgia Tech enters the game as a heavy underdog, facing a Georgia team that has dominated the series. The Jackets have lost the last eight games in this rivalry. Despite the lopsided history, Georgia Tech head coach Brent Key says his team refuses to roll over. He knows the Bulldogs well, and he knows his squad must execute a solid game plan to have any chance. A Season of Struggles The Yellow Jackets fell to Wake Forest at home in a 50-29 defeat. Wake Forest opened the game with 29 straight points and held the Jackets to just seven points in the first half. The defense allowed 607 total yards of offense, including 258 rushing yards for the opposing team. Georgia Tech turned the ball over three times, a mistake that cost them any hope of a comeback. Offensively, the Jackets struggled to find a rhythm until the second half. However, these individual efforts were not enough to overcome the defensive breakdowns. The team only averaged 6.3 yards per pass and failed to record a single sack against Wake Forest. Key’s Honest Assessment He acknowledged the difficulty of the task but promised his team would compete. “We’re going to show up, promise you that,” Key said. He emphasized that this is the most important game for his program because it is an in-state rivalry. Georgia Tech might still lose at Sanford Stadium even if they deliver their finest performance. The Bulldogs are the No. 1 team in the country, and they are looking to finish strong. Georgia Tech fans want to believe their team can cause a shock, but the reality of the season makes that unlikely. The Jackets have taken a significant step back, yet they remain dangerous if Georgia loses focus.

item.title: Kyle McCord’s 32.6 Rating Shows Miami Needs A Real Plan
item.description: Credit: Mark Konezny-Imagn Images Miami Dolphins fans saw a rough Sunday in Orchard Park as the team fell 26-9 to the Buffalo Bills. The final score looked close for a while, but the offense could not get going when it mattered most. Quarterback Kyle McCord threw for just 102 yards and one interception in his second start. Through Sunday’s games, the league’s lowest passer rating belonged to a quarterback at 32.6. The defense did enough to keep the game within reach for a long time. Safety Zayne Anderson earned a 90.8 grade from PFF for his work covering a short-handed secondary. An interception, a sack, and three pass breakups were his final stats. That effort helped hold Buffalo to field goals on three of their five red-zone trips. The Defense Stands Tall While the offense struggled, the defensive unit played with real energy. Rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez led the team with 13 combined tackles and added an interception. With 93 tackles, he currently holds the 7th spot in the National Football League. The group forced Josh Allen to throw two interceptions on the day. Head Coach Jeff Hafley explained the strategy against the Bills’ star quarterback. “We pressured him early and gave him a lot of different looks,” Hafley said of the plan against Allen, according to Yahoo Sports . He added that the rush and coverage worked well but noted there is still room for growth. “Rush plus coverage, I think that’s a pretty good day against Josh. But we can do better.” Offensive Woes Continue The offense could not take advantage of the defensive stops. Miami went 2 for 14 on third down and never reached the end zone. New kicker Daniel Carlson made all three of his field goals to score all nine of Miami’s points. Two of those kicks came from 52 yards out. McCord knew the offense was not close to good enough to win. “It’s tough to win games when you’re kicking field goals all day,” McCord said after the game. His receivers also had a tough time, with Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas combining for five drops. Douglas was targeted 10 times but only caught two passes for 30 yards. Hafley addressed the rookie receiver’s struggles after the loss. “Young player. It was one of those days,” Hafley said of Douglas. The coach noted that the play could have been huge for the rookie. “It could have been another huge day for him. It wasn’t.” The Dolphins now sit at 1-9 on the season after the loss. The team has shown they can fight, but they need more from their offense to win games. The front office will have to decide how much help to add around the quarterback this offseason. While time remains for growth for both Bell and Douglas, the front office will gain clearer insight this offseason regarding receiver additions needed around the drafted quarterback. Miami faces the New York Jets on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 1 p.m. ET at Hard Rock Stadium.

item.title: Women’s World Cup returns to U.S. in 2031 with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica as co-hosts
item.description: FIFA Women's World Cup hosting announcement What happened? The Women’s World Cup is coming back to the United States for the first time since 2003, and it’ll be the biggest edition yet. FIFA awarded the 2031 tournament to the U.S., Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica on Monday, marking the first time four countries will share hosting duties. The field will expand to 48 teams, with 104 matches on the schedule. FIFA also named the United Kingdom as host of the 2035 Women’s World Cup. 'Biggest most impactful Women's World Cup in history' 'Biggest most impactful Women's World Cup in history' In 2003, Cindy Parlow Cone scored in the USWNT’s World Cup opener against Sweden at RFK Stadium. Twenty-three years later, she was in Zurich as U.S. Soccer President, looking ahead to what the tournament’s return could mean for the next generation of players. “We are incredibly honored and excited to welcome the world to the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica for the 2031 FIFA Women’s World Cup,” Cone said. “This is a historic moment for our four countries, but the opportunity is much bigger than any one of us. Together with FIFA, we want to deliver the biggest and most impactful Women’s World Cup in history and use its success to accelerate the growth of women’s soccer around the world. Our ambition is to create a tournament that not only inspires millions of players, but helps give them the opportunities to play, grow and pursue their dreams.” What this means for the U.S. and the other federations While the U.S. has hosted Women's World Cups in the past, it hasn't done so since 2003. Before that, it was the 1999 Women's World Cup. While the U.S. have been here before, this is the first time that Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica will be hosting the women's tournament. "We have an opportunity to use the momentum from the 2031 FIFA Women’s World Cup to accelerate our ambitions for the future of soccer, from expanding access and participation to strengthening the pathways that develop the next generation of players," U.S. Soccer CEO and General Secretary JT Batson said. What's next? What's next? The 2031 Women’s World Cup will come five years after the men’s tournament in North America and three years after the Los Angeles Olympics. U.S. Soccer sees a chance to build on both events and bring more fans to the women’s game. With the four host countries set, the next question is which cities will get games. The joint bid put forward more than 30 candidates, and U.S. Soccer says the host cities and stadiums will be announced as planning moves forward.

item.title: Tarkowski's first Premier League red ruins Moyes' night - was it deserved?
item.description: It had been some run for Everton captain James Tarkowski. Prior to Monday night, the defender had received 74 yellow cards in the Premier League but had never been sent off - a top-flight record. But that run came to an end at Brentford as he was given his first red card in his 351st Premier League appearance, although the decision has attracted plenty of debate. His dismissal crucially means he will miss Sunday's Merseyside derby and also ruined David Moyes' record-breaking night as he took charge of his 593rd game as Everton boss - more than anyone else in the club's history. The 4-0 loss was also the heaviest defeat Everton have had since Moyes returned to the club at the start of last year. Tarkowski's dismissal proved a big talking point during and after the match, with opinions split on whether he should have gone. Even Moyes wasn't sure. He told BBC Match of the Day: "My thoughts at the time, I didn't think it was but when I've looked at it again I think his foot high. Is there enough force for it to be a red card? Not sure about that." James Tarkowski received his first Premier League red card [Getty Images] Why did Tarkowski get sent off? So what exactly happened? Just 15 minutes after Keane Lewis-Potter scored his second deflected strike of the evening, Everton skipper Tarkowski thundered into a challenge on Brentford's Yehor Yarmoliuk. He won the ball but also followed through with the challenge forcefully. Initially, referee Craig Pawson deemed a foul and a yellow card was enough. But, after an intervention from the video assistant referee (VAR) and studying the replay, Pawson changed the yellow for a red. The Premier League match centre said on X: "After VAR review, the referee overturned the original decision of yellow card for Tarkowski for the challenge on Yarmoliuk and issued a red card for serious foul play. "VAR: 'Point of contact is on the shin. He's got speed and intensity. Studs are high.' "REF: 'After review, Everton No.6 commits a challenge that endangers his opponent's safety, making contact with the studs onto the shin. Cancelling the yellow card - and a red card.'" 'Game's gone' or '100% red'? Experts are split Referees are asked to take into account several considerations for what counts as serious foul play including the speed of the challenge, its intensity, force and what degree of control there was. But, as always, there was plenty of debate about whether it was the correct decision. BBC Sport's football issues correspondent Dale Johnson, said: "Really not sure about this as a VAR red card. "Yes, Tarkowski absolutely ticks the boxes for speed and intensity and leading high with studs showing. "But the question marks are that Tarkowski made only small contact and didn't have a straight leg when he did so. "Maybe his reputation played a part? item.title: Brentford hit Everton for four to soar into Premier League top six
item.description: Keane Lewis-Potter scored twice in Brentford's win over Everton (Adrian DENNIS) Keane Lewis-Potter struck twice as Brentford battered 10-man Everton 4-0 to climb into the Premier League's top six on Monday. Lewis-Potter's luck was in as twice he saw deflected efforts leave Jordan Pickford stranded before a wild challenge by captain James Tarkowski left Everton a man down for over half the match. Vitaly Janelt's stunning strike from long range and Fabio Carvalho rounded off a comfortable victory for the Bees, who will fancy their chances when they travel to struggling Manchester United on Saturday. "It'll probably go a bit under the radar because of the sending off but 11 versus 11 we were outstanding," said Brentford boss Keith Andrews. "I'm really happy with the group, the club and long may it continue. "Long way to go. Onto Old Trafford on Saturday and we're really looking forward to it." David Moyes's record 593rd game as Everton boss was not one the Scot will want to remember as his side were swatted aside in west London despite having the chance to go fifth in the table. "With two shots, both deflected in and took the goalkeeper the wrong way, and the third goal was a worldie outside the box. We could use them as excuses but there's no excuses tonight," said Moyes. "The performance was way below the standards we've set and the way we've been playing recently." A defensive mix-up allowed Jaidon Anthony too much time to pick out Lewis-Potter for the opening goal and his shot deflected off Jarrad Branthwaite to wrong-foot Pickford. Two minutes later, Everton failed to deal with a free-kick into the box and Lewis-Potter was given two opportunities to double his tally. The winger's first effort was blocked by Tarkowski before Thierno Barry this time deflected into his own net as the Frenchman threw himself towards the ball. Worse was to come for the visitors when their skipper was shown red after a VAR review for catching Yehor Yarmoliuk on the shin. Tarkowski will now be banned for Sunday's Merseyside derby at home to Liverpool. Moyes turned to Jack Grealish off the bench at half-time in his first appearance since being dropped for breaching club discipline a month ago. Grealish could do little to inspire the 10 men as Janelt's strike lit up an otherwise uneventful second half. The German midfielder blasted into the top corner from well outside the box 23 minutes from time. Carvalho rounded off the scoring from point-blank range when a corner fell to the former Liverpool winger in the 90th minute. Brentford will head to Old Trafford for Mauricio Pochettino's first home match in charge of United full of confidence and eager to inflict more woe on the Red Devils. United sit second bottom of the table after a nine-game winless league run, plunging the English giants into danger of being relegated for the first time in 52 years. kca/iwd

item.title: Kerby Joseph escapes debut with 'no red flags,' good to go vs Bears
item.description: Kerby Joseph's season debut went off without a hitch, and the Detroit Lions safety looks ready to play on short rest on Thanksgiving against the Chicago Bears. "There’s no red flags, so that’s a good sign," Lions coach Dan Campbell said Monday, Nov. 23. "He got over 40 reps, so that was good. That’s a good sign. And so he’ll be better for those reps, just like [Brian] Branch was to get his first set of reps for the season." Joseph played 46 snaps (67%) as the Lions' third safety in Sunday's 31-21 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , his first game since October 2025 because of a cartilage condition in his knee. BAND OF BROTHERS: How Lions defense has come together to suddenly be one of NFL's stingiest units He made one tackle on a bubble screen, was credited with another when he tagged Baker Mayfield down after a scramble and lined up almost exclusively as a deep safety in the Lions' nickel package, with Branch and Chuck Clark also on the field. Campbell said last week Joseph looked good in practice, but the Lions needed to see how he responded to back-to-back days of work and how he recovered from game action before deciding how to use him going forward. Clark wore the green-dot defensive communication helmet and played every snap against the Bucs , and Branch, who returned last month from a torn Achilles suffered late in the 2025 season, was on the field for 68 of 69 defensive plays. The Lions play the Bears on Thursday (1 p.m., CBS) with three days rest this week, then have a long weekend before getting into the homestretch of their schedule with games against the Atlanta Falcons, Tennessee Titans , Minnesota Vikings , New York Giants , Bears again and Green Bay Packers . "I thought he did some good things," Campbell said. "There’s things that he’s going to only just get better at now that he’s been out there and I thought it was pretty good. I mean, when you’re able to get he and BB on the field and you got Chuck out there, it’s a pretty good unit." Dave Birkett covers the Lions for the Detroit Free Press. item.title: Jameson Williams Responds to Controversial Touchdown Flip
item.description: Detroit Lions wide receiver Jameson Williams has never been shy about showing off his personality, but his latest touchdown celebration had plenty of fans holding their breath. During Sunday’s 31-21 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Ford Field, Williams hauled in a 57-yard touchdown pass from Jared Goff before launching himself into a front flip as he crossed the goal line. The problem? Williams didn’t exactly stick the landing, and the timing couldn’t have been much worse considering what happened to teammate Aidan Hutchinson just one week earlier. Following the game, Williams was asked about his decision to attempt the risky celebration. His response was about as Jameson Williams as it gets. Detroit Lions wide receiver Jameson Williams (1) makes a catch for a touchdown against Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the second half at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Jameson Williams Explains His Controversial Celebration Speaking with reporters following Detroit’s sixth consecutive victory, Williams admitted that the flip wasn’t exactly something he had carefully planned. “The flip was, like, an in-the-moment thing, I ain’t gonna lie,” Williams said, according to The Detroit News . Williams also acknowledged that he hadn’t been entirely sure what to do as he approached the end zone. Fortunately, the awkward landing didn’t prevent him from finishing the game. But here’s where things get interesting. According to Parker Hurley of Heavy , Williams apparently has no intention of permanently retiring the celebration. “I’m going to try to land one later in the year for y’all, for sure,” Williams said. Yep, it sounds like Jamo might give it another shot. Aidan Hutchinson’s Injury Makes Williams’ Flip More Concerning The controversy surrounding Williams’ celebration stems from what happened to Hutchinson during Detroit’s November 15 victory over the New England Patriots in Germany. Hutchinson suffered a season-ending torn ACL after jumping into the air and landing awkwardly while celebrating a sack. The devastating injury immediately sparked conversations about whether NFL players should reconsider potentially dangerous celebrations. However, Lions head coach Dan Campbell made his position on touchdown celebrations clear , explaining that he wasn’t interested in policing how his players celebrate. That doesn’t necessarily mean Williams’ flip was a great idea, particularly with Detroit preparing for an important Thanksgiving showdown against the Chicago Bears. Williams has become one of Detroit’s most dangerous offensive weapons, and the Lions certainly can’t afford to lose another impact player because of an unnecessary injury. Of course, Williams’ performance Sunday provided another reminder of why he’s so valuable to Detroit’s offense. item.title: Here are the Big Ten’s 4 paths for Indiana to reach its championship game
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - DECEMBER 06: Head coach Curt Cignetti of the Indiana Hoosiers lifts the trophy after defeating the Ohio State Buckeyes 13-10 in the 2025 Big Ten Football Championship at Lucas Oil Stadium on December 06, 2025 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Indiana football, despite a pair of losses in conference play, is still alive in the race for a bid in the Big Ten Championship Game. The game, set for Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, will be the league’s last. Conference title games will be discontinued under the newly-expanded College Football Playoff starting with the 2027 season. This is the Hoosiers’ last chance to win another conference championship in their home state. Indiana is still alive, but doesn’t control its own destiny. There’s too many teams bunched around the top for the Hoosiers to make it in with just a win over Purdue, but said win is vital to their chances. Without a win over the Boilermakers, no path exists for Indiana to male the conference championship. I dug in last night and attempted to map out some paths for Indiana to some level of success. The Big Ten has been doing the same. Here are its official paths for the Hoosiers: Indiana will reach the 2026 Big Ten Football Championship Game if… Iowa loses to Nebraska AND Oregon loses to Washington OR Iowa defeats Nebraska, Oregon loses to Washington AND UCLA loses to USC OR Oregon defeats Washington, Iowa loses to Nebraska AND UCLA loses to USC OR Iowa defeats Nebraska, Oregon defeats Washington, Minnesota defeats Wisconsin AND UCLA loses to USC Those are Indiana’s four paths. All depend on the Hoosiers beating the Boilermakers on Saturday night. Indiana needs various results to win out in tiebreaker scenarios against fellow 2-loss teams, either with a superior record against common opponents or a higher cumulative winning percentage from shared opponents in the event of a tied record, which is the case with Iowa. Here’s the times and dates for those games important to Indiana’s chances: Nebraska at Iowa (12 p.m. ET on Friday, November 27) Minnesota at Wisconsin (7:30 p.m. on Friday, November 27) USC at UCLA (3:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, November 28) Purdue at Indiana (7 p.m. ET on Saturday, November 28) Washington at Oregon (7:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, November 28) Join the conversation! Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Indiana fans and fans across the country. Indiana football’s 27-24 overtime loss at Washington was the Hoosiers’ second on the season, moving them to 9-2 overall and 6-2 in conference play. Their first loss came several weeks earlier, at home in a similarly closely contested game against Ohio State. Losing one time was a hit the Hoosiers could take while still feeling good about their chances at a third consecutive College Football Playoff berth. A second loss puts them in significant jeopardy heading into the final week of the season with few opportunities for a makeup. We’ve seen multiple two-loss teams miss the 12-team playoff before. Miami and BYU missed out on a bid in 2024 and Notre Dame was notoriously left out of the field in favor of Miami in 2025. The 2026 field doesn’t appear as strong as that of either 2024 or 2024, but Indiana is in jeopardy regardless. The updated rankings will be released tomorrow evening. item.title: Willie Green And Dusty May Built A Rare Coaching Bond In Dallas
item.description: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Willie Green and Dusty May share a connection that goes far beyond a standard coach and assistant role. The Dallas Mavericks have found a rare spark in their leadership pair, one that started on a golf course in Michigan. The bond influences the team’s culture. Green, the lead assistant, and May, the head coach, operate with a trust that most staffs spend years trying to build. They hit it off immediately, acting like long-lost friends from their first meeting. That instant chemistry is now the foundation of a 10-7 team heading into Tuesday’s NBA Cup game in Denver. A Golf Outing That Changed Everything Their story began when a mutual friend invited both men to play golf in Michigan. Green was born and raised in Detroit, while May had just finished a stint at the University of Michigan. They were introduced on the course. Green noted that such quick connections are rare in the NBA world. “Rarely does that happen,” Green said. “But when it does you recognize it pretty quickly, and our energy is kind of moving in the same direction.” This shared energy allows them to bounce ideas off each other constantly, creating a collaborative environment that benefits the entire roster. Green brings a specific weight to the table as the only former head coach on May’s staff. He previously led the New Orleans Pelicans and served as an assistant for the Golden State Warriors and Phoenix Suns. With the Warriors, he secured two NBA titles in 2017 and 2018. May relies heavily on this background, asking Green questions daily about both the player and coach mindset. “I ask those guys a number of questions every day from the mindset of a player, and then also from the mindset of a coach because they’ve done both,” May said, according to NBA.com . More Than Just a Coaching Staff The relationship extends past strategy and into the daily grind of the team. Green describes May as a hard worker who is often one of the first people in the building. “He’s a hard worker (and) one of the first guys in here,” Green said. The respect is mutual, with Green calling the experience incredible as they learn from one another. This dynamic has helped the Mavericks assemble a young, hungry group that feels connected. May also relies on Garrett Temple, who ended a 17-year NBA career before becoming part of the staff. Together, Green and Temple provide the most NBA experience available to the coaching group. They cover the gap between old-school grit and new-school tactics. This mix helps the team navigate the highs and lows of a long season. The result is a squad that can guard multiple positions and plays with a chip on their shoulder. item.title: Atlanta Dream Must Fix Roster Flaws Before 2027 Season
item.description: David Gonzales-Imagn Images The Golden State Valkyries defeated the Atlanta Dream in Game 7 of the WNBA Finals, leaving the Dream one win short of a championship. While the franchise reached its first Finals since 2013, the path to a title demands more than just repeating the same roster. Shooting Woes Stopped the Dream Atlanta was elite in several categories last year, including rebounding and defense, yet the team could not close out the series. The main issue was shooting beyond the arc. The Dream ranked 11th overall in 3-point shooting percentage at 32.5 percent, a number too low for a contender. Even star players struggled to find their rhythm when it mattered most. Rhyne Howard shot 35.5 percent during the regular season but dropped to 30.4 percent in the postseason. Angel Reese and Jordin Canada also missed their marks from deep, with percentages of 19.3 and 29.2 respectively. General manager Dan Padover proved his worth by landing Angel Reese, but that single move is not enough to beat the best teams in the league. High Post Hoops notes that while Padover touches gold, the roster needs a dedicated 3-point shooter to balance the attack. Retaining DeWanna Bonner would help, but the team needs more depth to survive a grueling schedule. Adding a player like Chennedy Carter could be a high-risk, high-reward move that changes the dynamic of the bench. Ownership and Arena Logistics The team faces business hurdles that may affect on‑court performance unless they are addressed. The Dream will move all 25 home games to State Farm Arena in 2027, a shift that requires careful planning. The 2026 postseason created a logistical headache because the venue already had major events booked. To prevent another chaotic scramble, the league has instituted strict rules for the 2027 season. Teams that fail to report these issues risk losing home playoff games or facing financial fines. A Sisterhood Built to Last The team president said the journey mattered beyond the final score. Morgan Shaw Parker, the team President and Chief Operating Officer, thanked fans for their support during the championship run. In a letter to supporters, she emphasized the bond formed within the city. “We didn’t just rebuild a basketball team. We rebuilt a connection with our city,” she wrote, according to CBS News . Despite admitting the letdown, Parker encouraged supporters to appreciate the community that grew around the franchise. She also highlighted the long-term vision for the organization despite the missing trophy. “We may not have finished this season with a championship, but we have built a franchise Atlanta can be proud of, a community worth protecting, and a sisterhood worth believing in,” she wrote.

item.title: Talor Gooch Faces Harsh Reality As LIV Golf Folds
item.description: John (Jack) Power-Imagn Images Talor Gooch secured four wins and over $72 million in prize money during the LIV Golf era, yet he now faces a stark silence regarding his future. The 35-year-old finds himself in a unique position where past financial success offers little protection against current exclusion. The road back to the PGA Tour looks incredibly steep for the former RSM Classic winner. He has played in six majors since LIV began in 2022, missing the cut three times and never finishing higher than 34th. That track record does not inspire confidence among tournament directors who have the power to grant invites. A Different Path Than Chacarra Other defectors are finding success by returning to competitive golf, but their stories highlight Gooch’s struggle. Full exempt status on the PGA Tour for 2027 is held by Eugenio Chacarra, who secured three victories on the DP World Tour in 2026. Chacarra admitted he lost motivation while on LIV but regained his hunger after leaving the Saudi-backed circuit. “You know, I lost those things my last year with LIV, and I earned it back by leaving, by working hard, by showing the world what I’m capable of, and I’m more hungry than ever,” Chacarra said. Chacarra plans to face 33 players ahead of him in the world rankings as he aims for the Ryder Cup. He has a clear plan to get better over the next 30 days before his first start at Torrey Pines. Gooch lacks this kind of clear momentum. He took on a leadership role for LIV after Brooks Koepka left, rebranding his team to OKGC, but that leadership role dissolved when the league itself folded. Uncertain Future for the Leader Not every player wants to grind through a full global schedule, and some are choosing a lighter load. Marc Leishman, a former Ripper GC teammate of Cameron Smith, said he is “past the grind” of being away from his family for more than half the year. Ahead of the Australian PGA Championship in Sydney, Leishman stated to reporters that he holds no regrets regarding his decision to join LIV despite the uncertainty surrounding his future. “Obviously, it’s a little uncertain what the future holds for me, but if I knew exactly what was going to happen, I would have made the same decision. I’ve certainly got no regrets,” Leishman said. Instead of pursuing a full card, Leishman intends to focus on major championships and events in his homeland. Gooch does not have this luxury. He was once a figure of ridicule for comparing LIV events to the Ryder Cup, despite never having played in either. The silence surrounding his next move suggests the golf world has moved on. He is third on LIV’s all-time money list, but that ranking holds little value in the current landscape.

item.title: Conor Orr explains why Deshaun Watson winning NFL Comeback Player of the Year 'can't happen'
item.description: Nov 15, 2026; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson (4) celebrates after defeating the Houston Texans at Huntington Bank Field. Mandatory Credit: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images As we inch closer to the end of the 2026 NFL season, discussions around major awards have begun. There’s still plenty of football left to play, but pundits and fans are already arguing over who’ll win MVP, Rookie of the Year, Defensive Player of the Year, and more. There’s one award, however, that already has a lot of people sweating over who might take home the hardware. The NFL Comeback Player of the Year award. To be fair, Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes seems to have the inside track to win the award if he keeps putting up similar numbers. He’s an ideal candidate, having recovered from major knee surgery and put together numbers that recall some of his Super Bowl-caliber seasons. However, there’s also another candidate who, on paper, could make a case. Quarterback Deshaun Watson has returned from nearly two years away after Achilles surgeries, leading the Cleveland Browns to a 6–4 record so far in the AFC North playoff hunt. Of course, Watson also comes with a whole lot of baggage in the form of over two dozen lawsuits amid accusations of sexual assault and misconduct , often displaying a stunning lack of introspection or ownership about something NFL commissioner Roger Goodell referred to as “egregious” and “predatory behavior.” But Watson has also benefited from a friendly NFL media (though not everyone ) that has helped rehab his image by talking around those issues , since his on-field performance has been good. All of which has Sports Illustrated’s Conor Orr feeling like Watson winning Comeback Player of the Year simply “can’t happen.” “If everything holds and there’s a stasis in the NFL between now and the end of the season, this award is going to tear us limb from limb,” Orr told Albert Breer on the latest episode of The MMQB. “I think the NFL is like, ‘Please, God, Patrick Mahomes, finish the season healthy so we can just give this to you.'” Orr referenced that Damar Hamlin didn’t win Comeback Player of the Year as part of his argument that giving Watson the award would send a terrible message. “Imagine a world where a human being ceases to be alive on the field. comes back and plays in an NFL game, and does not win Comeback Player of the Year, and Deshaun Watson wins Comeback Player of the Year, all in a span of a half decade. item.title: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟
item.description: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟 Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan has capped a record-setting regular season by being named the 2026 MLS Young Player of the Year. In his first full campaign, the Man City-bound starlet emerged as one of the league's most exciting young talents, finishing with with a career-high 23 goal contributions (nine goals, 14 assists) in 29 appearances, and recorded a goal contribution in 10 consecutive matches, the longest such run by a teenager in MLS history. Both his total of 23 goal contributions and his 14 assists are the most ever by a teenager in a single MLS season. Sullivan's form also earned him MLS Player of the Month honors for September 2026. At 17 years and two days old, he became the youngest winner of the award in league history. His production on the club level soon translated to the international stage. Sullivan received his first call-up to the US men's national team in September and made his debut against Peru, becoming the second-youngest player in USMNT history to start a match. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.)
